TikTok Shop analytics tools exist to answer research questions: what is selling, which creators drive it, and which videos are going viral right now. Kalodata is the best-known, but it is one of several, and analytics tools are a different category from outreach and management software. If your job is deciding what to sell and who sells it, analytics is what you need. If your job is contacting creators, that is a different tool.

What analytics tools do

They surface market data you cannot easily see inside your own Seller Center:

  • Trending products across categories, so you spot demand early.
  • Top creators by GMV and category, for research and shortlisting.
  • Viral videos and livestreams, to reverse-engineer what content converts.
  • Category and competitor benchmarks, so you know where you stand.

This is decision support, not execution. Analytics tells you what to do; it does not do it.

Product research is the use case creators reach for most. Popular walkthroughs test platforms like ShopShark, described as "a TikTok Shop analytics and product research platform built for creators, affiliates, sellers, and brands who want to find winning products" (creator review on YouTube). That is the core job of this category: surface what is selling so you are not guessing.

The main options

  • Kalodata is the category leader for TikTok Shop product, creator, and video analytics.
  • FastMoss and similar tools cover overlapping ground on trending products and creator data.
  • The full affiliate platforms (Reacher, Euka, Cruva) include analytics alongside outreach, if you want both in one place.

Pricing and features shift, so check current plans before committing.

Analytics vs outreach vs management

Be clear on what you are buying:

  • Analytics = research (Kalodata). What sells, who sells it.
  • Discovery = building a creator shortlist (discovery tools).
  • Outreach and management = contacting and running creators (affiliate software).

Many brands over-buy here, paying for a full platform when they only needed product research, or buying analytics when their real gap was execution.

How to choose

  • Deciding what to sell or which creators exist: an analytics tool like Kalodata.
  • Building a contact shortlist: a discovery tool.
  • Running the whole program: full affiliate software, or a managed agency that does the research and the execution.

The takeaway

Analytics tools are for research: trending products, top creators, viral content. They are essential for deciding what and who, and useless for the doing. Pair them with execution tooling or a team, and do not confuse knowing with acting.

Want the research and the execution handled together? Book a call, or find creators in the categories your research surfaces.
